transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I keep swinging between eating way too much and then trying to "make up for it" with these harsh rules and routines, and it’s starting to take over my days. My primary doctor noticed this pattern and urged me to talk with someone before it gets any worse as I head toward retirement.
When you try to "make up" for eating too much, what specific methods do you use—for example, do you make yourself throw up, use laxatives, fast, or exercise excessively?

I don't throw up or take any pills. Instead, I force myself to go on long, punishing walks the next day and strictly limit what I eat, sometimes surviving on just coffee and an apple. I feel like I have to "balance the books" this way, even when I'm exhausted and starving.
To help me understand your situation better, could you share your current height and weight, and whether you've recently experienced significant weight loss?

I don't know my exact height and weight off the top of my head, to be honest. However, my primary care doctor did notice that my weight has been fluctuating quite a bit recently, which is part of why he suggested I come see you.
Even though you don't know your exact weight, would you say you are currently underweight, or has your doctor expressed concern that your weight is too low?

No, my doctor hasn't said my weight is too low, he just noticed it fluctuating up and down. I definitely don't feel underweight at all. In fact, when I look in the mirror, I feel like I'm just getting soft.
How often do these episodes of eating too much and then trying to 'make up for it' happen in a typical week, and how many months has this been going on?
These episodes happen at least once or twice every week. This entire cycle has been going on for about four months now, starting right around the time I transitioned to my reduced work schedule.
During these times when you eat way too much, do you experience a feeling of loss of control, where you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you are eating?

Yes, I definitely feel a complete loss of control. It feels like a switch clicks off in my brain where I'll tell myself to stop, but my hands just keep reaching for food on autopilot. I only really snap out of it when I realize I'm uncomfortably full.
Do you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and do you set a strict target weight for yourself that is very low?

I don't really have a specific target weight in mind, and I'm not sure if I would call it an intense fear of gaining weight. However, I definitely struggle with feeling "soft" and being very unhappy with my shape when I look in the mirror.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you judge yourself as a person? Does it play a major role in your overall self-esteem?

It plays a massive role in my self-esteem. Even when my wife tells me I look fine, I'll stand in front of the mirror pinching my stomach and thinking I'm getting soft and useless. That thought pretty much decides whether I've had a good or bad day, regardless of what else I actually accomplished.

Because he lacks a specific low target weight or a classic morbid dread of fatness (though he has significant body shape overvaluation), both Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) and Atypical Bulimia Nervosa (F50.3) remain the primary diagnostic candidates. final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a subjective loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (excessive exercise and severe dietary restriction) occurring 1-2 times per week for 4 months. Although these symptoms cause significant distress and heavily influence self-esteem, the patient does not meet the full criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) because they lack a morbid dread of fatness and do not set a sharply defined, abnormally low weight threshold. Therefore, the clinical presentation is best classified as Atypical Bulimia Nervosa (F50.3).
